title: ACE dispersed-base sortie-generation logistics C2 under degraded communications (decentralized fuel, munitions, spares and airmen decisions at hub-and-spoke locations)
problem: Air Force wings executing Agile Combat Employment (ACE) from hub-and-spoke locations must make fuel, munitions, spares, maintenance and airmen allocation decisions while cut off from centralized, pull-based maintenance and supply systems, and no fielded software encodes those decentralized (conditional-authority) decisions or reconciles them when links return.
echelons: air expeditionary wing / mission generation force element

user.exact_role: Maintenance Group / Logistics Readiness Squadron leaders and Wing A4 staff (mission generation force element commander, production superintendent, fuels and munitions flight chiefs, multi-capable airmen team leads) at ACE spokes
organization_examples: Pacific Air Forces wings (e.g., 18th Wing Kadena, 35th FW Misawa)
USAFE-AFAFRICA wings (e.g., 48th FW Lakenheath; 48th MXG cited by LOA on speed of maintenance decisions)
Air Combat Command 505th Command and Control Wing (Logistics C2 experimentation)

current_workflow: Before dispersal: wing plans spokes, pre-positions fuel/munitions/spares kits; status lives in enterprise systems (maintenance information systems such as IMDS/G081-class and supply ILS-S-class, accessed over NIPRNet) - system names RECALL, not re-verified this session

At the spoke: multi-capable airmen generate sorties; status is tracked on whiteboards, spreadsheets and radio/chat reports when connectivity is intermittent (INFERENCE from LOGTAC and REFORPAC reporting)

Decisions that exceed local authority (cannibalization, munitions cross-load, fuel rationing, deferring maintenance) are escalated to the hub or MAJCOM via whatever comms exist; 2025 CAF LOGTAC built 'conditional authorities' frameworks so lower echelons can decide without escalation

When links return, spoke status is manually reconciled into enterprise systems; airlift/resupply requests flow through separate logistics C2 channels (the 505th CCW's 2026 Logistics C2 Hackathon targeted the unit-requirement-to-airlift-execution seam)
current_solution: Doctrine (AFDN 1-21 ACE) plus tactics development (CAF LOGTAC 2025 conditional authorities), enterprise analytics for maintenance (RSO PANDA/CBM+ toolkit; BLADE - RECALL), government experimentation (505th CCW Logistics C2 Hackathon, June 2026), exercise-driven workarounds during REFORPAC 2025, and now an AFWERX Phase I SBIR to Rune Technologies (July 2026) to adapt its TyrOS logistics C2 platform to ACE. No product of record found at the spoke.
failure: The enterprise maintenance/supply stack is centralized and pull-based and assumes connectivity; at a disconnected spoke there is no tool that (a) holds an authoritative local picture of fuel, munitions, spares and airmen, (b) encodes the conditional authorities/decision thresholds developed at LOGTAC, and (c) syncs and reconciles with hub systems when a link returns. Decisions therefore stall on escalation or are made on whiteboards without an audit trail.

evidence.claim: AFDN 1-21 Agile Combat Employment names logistics under attack as a key ACE element and describes a shift from pull-based to push-based, dispersed sustainment.
evidence.source_title: Air Force Doctrine Note 1-21, Agile Combat Employment (1 Dec 2021; reissued 23 Aug 2022)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The inaugural Combat Air Forces Logistics Tactical Conference (Nellis AFB, April 2025) stood up a Conditional Authorities working group that developed frameworks for decentralized, risk-informed decision-making in sortie generation under degraded C2; the next LOGTAC is planned for spring 2027 (tactics development, not a procurement).
evidence.source_title: CAF LOGTAC: Forging Lethal Logistics for the Future Fight (Logistics Officer Association); Inaugural CAF LOGTAC advances combat logistics, readiness (ACC)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The DoD Inspector General announced (5 May 2025) an evaluation of the extent to which the Air Force implemented logistics requirements for ACE in the Indo-Pacific (fieldwork at PACAF and ACC). Final report not located this session - Public evidence insufficient on findings.
evidence.source_title: Project Announcement D2025-DEV0PE-0108.000, Evaluation of the U.S. Air Force's Implementation of Logistics Requirements for ACE in the Indo-Pacific Region
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: AFWERX selected Rune Technologies for a Phase I SBIR to apply its TyrOS platform to AI-enabled logistics command and control for ACE (announced 30 Jul 2026). A Phase I award is a feasibility study, not a deployment; but it shows the Air Force is already funding a venture-backed startup on exactly this gap.
evidence.source_title: Rune Technologies Selected by U.S. Air Force to Advance AI-Enabled Logistics for Agile Combat Employment (Business Wire)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Rune Technologies closed a $24M Series A (Jul 2025), won a five-year $99M Army IDIQ for TyrOS (Jun 2026; IDIQ ceiling, not revenue), joined USMC Project Dynamis as sole logistics C2 provider (May 2026) and received $4.1M from the Army for 1st Cavalry Division autonomous resupply (Sep 2026) - a well-funded competitor already occupies contested-logistics C2 across three services.
evidence.source_title: Business Wire / Defense Post coverage of Rune Technologies (2025-2026)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: REFORPAC (10 Jul - 8 Aug 2025) put roughly 300-400 aircraft across ~25 locations and, per PACAF's commander, forced planners to innovate around ACE logistics and C2 at a scale not previously tried; DLA described it as stress-testing ACE logistics and 'the friction of distribution'.
evidence.source_title: What PACAF Boss Took Away from REFORPAC Exercise (Air & Space Forces Magazine); Stars and Stripes 2025-07-21; DLA 'REFORPAC 2025 and the friction of distribution'
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: ACC's 505th Command and Control Wing hosted a Logistics C2 Hackathon (reported 4 Jun 2026) to accelerate decision timelines from unit-level logistics requirement generation to tactical airlift execution - government-led experimentation on the same seam (article text not fetched; egress blocked).
evidence.source_title: Air Force Forges Decision Advantage Through Logistics C2 Hackathon (Soldier Systems Daily)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: RAND (PAF) modeled how distributed maintenance postures affect PACAF sortie-rate potential under ACE, and separately found airmen are confused about ACE roles and combat-support staffing is short - independent, government-sponsored evidence that dispersed sortie generation is a live analytic and manning problem, not only a software problem.
evidence.source_title: RAND RRA999-3 Assessing ACE for PACAF: Distributed Maintenance Postures and Sortie Rate Potential; RAND RRA3169-1 Developing Combat Support Mission Ready Airmen for ACE
evidence.pub_date: date not verified this session (2023-2025 range)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Mitchell Institute (Mar 2025) argues logistics while under attack is central to CCA force design; Air University research describes institutional obstacles to flexible logistics and degraded resupply.
evidence.source_title: Logistics While Under Attack: Key to a CCA Force Design (Mitchell Institute); Flexible Logistics and Degraded Resupply (Air University)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: No discrete DAF budget line for ACE spoke-level logistics C2 software was found; the FY2026 DAF O&M justification exists but was not parsed for an ACE logistics IT line this session. Public evidence insufficient.
evidence.source_title: Department of the Air Force FY2026 Budget Estimates, O&M Vol I (June 2025)
evidence.label: INFERENCE

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Until mid-2026 no startup had a funded Air Force entry point: the pain surfaced in doctrine, RAND studies and exercises, none of which are buyers, and the maintenance/supply data needed to make a spoke tool useful sits in government-controlled legacy systems under a different program office (AFLCMC / RSO) than the tactics owners (ACC A4, PACAF A4). Rune Technologies (Anduril alumni, $24M Series A) has now taken the obvious position via an AFWERX Phase I (July 2026) after first winning Army and USMC vehicles - i.e., the gap was reachable only by a team with existing logistics-C2 product, service relationships and capital, and it is being addressed by exactly such a team (FACT for the awards; INFERENCE for the causal story).
technical_wedge: An offline-first, edge-synchronized 'sortie-generation logistics board' for a spoke: local ledger of fuel, munitions, spares/cann candidates and airmen availability; a rules layer that encodes CAF LOGTAC-style conditional authorities (who may decide what, at which thresholds, with what risk flags); CRDT-style reconciliation to hub systems when links return; and an export of decisions and requests into the airlift/resupply C2 chain. Technically ordinary; the value is in the encoded authorities and the integration, not the software.

mvp.what: Tablet/laptop app plus small sync service: spoke status ledger, conditional-authority decision aid with audit trail, store-and-forward sync over intermittent links (simulated with network impairment), and a hub dashboard that merges N spokes.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes with simulated data: a 4-spoke, 72-hour synthetic ACE vignette showing decisions made locally under link loss, reconciled without conflicts on reconnect, and a resupply request generated; could be shown at a PACAF/USAFE Spark cell or an AFWERX Spark Collider-type event.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That decentralized decisions with encoded authorities are faster and better audited than escalation-by-radio, that reconciliation with hub records is conflict-free, and that maintainers will actually enter status into it under field conditions (adoption is the real risk).

data_requirement.what: Unit-level status: aircraft maintenance status and parts (from maintenance information systems), fuel on hand and burn rates, munitions inventory and build status, airmen qualifications and duty status; plus the authority matrices produced at LOGTAC (likely CUI or FOUO).
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Initially only as synthetic data; real feeds require a government sponsor, CUI handling and, for maintenance data, cooperation from the AFLCMC/RSO data owners. Conditional-authority matrices from LOGTAC are not public. Realistic for a SBIR awardee with a sponsoring wing; not obtainable for an unsponsored two-student team.

customer.contract_signer: AFWERX (AFRL contracting) for SBIR; a MAJCOM contracting squadron for a Spark-cell purchase

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR requires >50% ownership and control by U.S. citizens or permanent residents; the German founder as a future permanent resident may qualify, but an Indonesian non-U.S.-person co-founder's equity and control must be structured carefully (needs SBIR-eligibility counsel). CUI/IL4 handling and potential ITAR exposure (munitions data) may restrict a non-U.S.-person's access to the very data the product needs - describe to counsel; no legal judgment made here.

Adjacent: Army Vantage / EA for readiness and logistics data; Air Force footprint (RECALL); could extend Foundry ontology to spoke workflows via forward-deployed engineers.

competition.evidence: RECALL - not re-verified this session; confidence LOW

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes. Palantir can add spoke-level logistics objects to an existing Air Force Foundry deployment in months; Anduril's Lattice Mesh already solves the degraded-transport half; Rune is a startup incumbent that has the product and is now funded for this exact use case. Government software factories can also build the workflow in-house (hackathon).
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject. A new entrant offers no data, no interface control, no service relationships and no product lead; the defensible piece (encoded conditional authorities) is government intellectual property produced at LOGTAC that any awardee would receive from the sponsor.

capital_required.proof_of_concept_usd: 40,000-80,000 (two founders, synthetic vignette, offline-first app, 3-5 months)
capital_required.credible_military_demo_usd: 250,000-600,000 (requires a sponsoring wing or Phase I/II SBIR, exercise participation, CUI handling, an ex-maintenance-officer advisor, IL4 hosting)
capital_required.first_production_deployment_usd: 3,000,000-8,000,000 (Phase II/III, ATO on DAF cloud, integration with maintenance and supply data via RSO, multi-wing rollout) - and no program office of record to fund it
capital_required.assumptions: Assumes AFWERX SBIR eligibility is resolved; assumes RSO grants data access; assumes ACC A4 sponsors; all three are unproven. INFERENCE.

expertise_required.role: Former Air Force aircraft maintenance officer or senior maintenance/LRS SNCO with ACE exercise experience
expertise_required.why: Defines the real decision thresholds, knows IMDS/G081 realities and who decides what at a spoke; without this the product is a generic checklist app
Conflict-free sync over intermittent tactical links is the technical core

expertise_required.role: DAF software acquisition / AFWERX navigator (ex-Kessel Run, RSO or Spark cell)
expertise_required.why: Finds the sponsor, the memorandum and the transition path that does not currently exist
Maintenance and munitions data are CUI; ATO on Cloud One/Platform One is the gate to any real data

regulatory_burden.explanation: Unclassified start; CUI handling and IL4/IL5 ATO required for any real data; munitions-related technical data may carry ITAR/EAR implications; CMMC Level 2 likely for follow-on contracts. No classified data needed for the wedge.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person co-founder cannot be assumed eligible to access CUI munitions/maintenance data or to count toward SBIR ownership; corporate structure (control, board, ownership) must be reviewed by SBIR and export-control counsel. Not a legal judgment.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Offline-first field operations logging exists commercially (mining, utilities, disaster response) with entrenched vendors; the differentiator here (conditional military authorities, sortie generation) has no commercial analog.

defensibility.explanation: Weak: the encoded authorities are government-derived; integrations are brokered by AFLCMC and could be handed to any vendor; no data network effects at spoke scale. Rune's early relationships and multi-service vehicles are the kind of moat a new entrant would be trying to build from zero.

why_now: ACE became doctrine (2021-2022), REFORPAC 2025 scaled it to hundreds of aircraft and dozens of sites, CAF LOGTAC (Apr 2025) produced the first conditional-authority frameworks, the DoD IG opened an ACE-logistics evaluation (May 2025), the 505th CCW ran a Logistics C2 hackathon (2026) and AFWERX funded Rune for ACE logistics C2 (Jul 2026). The window for a first mover opened in 2025 and is already being filled.
killer_risk: There is no requirement owner with a budget line, no program office of record, and the only funded vehicle (AFWERX Phase I) has just been awarded to a venture-backed startup with $24M and multi-service contracts for exactly this use case; a two-student team would be entering as a second-mover on a government-controlled data problem with a customer whose main pain relief comes from tactics and manning changes, not software.

procurement_signal_timeline.event: AFDN 1-21 ACE published (1 Dec 2021; updated Aug 2022) naming logistics under attack
RSO CBM+ AI toolkit (PANDA) designated Air Force System of Record - enterprise predictive maintenance, not spoke C2
CAF LOGTAC (Apr) conditional authorities; DoD IG ACE logistics evaluation announced (May); REFORPAC (Jul-Aug) stress-tests ACE logistics; Rune $24M Series A (Jul)

Kessel Run Next-Gen AOC program launched (Feb); Rune joins USMC Project Dynamis (May) and wins $99M Army IDIQ (Jun); 505th CCW Logistics C2 Hackathon (Jun); AFWERX Phase I to Rune for ACE logistics C2 (Jul); next CAF LOGTAC set for spring 2027

allied_extension: Somewhat: NATO air forces and Australia are adopting ACE-like dispersal (JAPCC writes on ACE; RAAF and USAFE partners exercise it), and allied buyers are less locked into U.S. maintenance systems, which could make a spoke tool easier to integrate. But allied procurement is slower, each air force has its own maintenance IT, and the founders' German/Indonesian mix does not by itself open Bundeswehr or RAAF doors. It does not rescue the U.S. case.
